title: 1.4.17 Where Does the Balance Live?
description: Five multiple-choice questions on where behaviour lives in procedural versus object-oriented style. Checked instantly.

questions.question: A program tracks a bank account balance and needs code that deposits money into it. In object-oriented style, where does the depositing code live?
options: Inside the account object, alongside the balance it changes
In a separate variable next to the balance
Anywhere in the file — object-oriented style does not care
In a comment above the balance
questions.explanation: The behaviour goes where the data is. The account holds the balance and knows how to deposit into it.

questions.question: What is it about that arrangement that makes the style object-oriented?
options: The code ends up shorter than it would otherwise be
The program runs faster
The variable names are longer and more descriptive
Data and the behaviour that operates on it are bundled into one value
questions.explanation: Bundling is the whole idea — properties and methods in one object, per Definition 1.4.4.

questions.question: In procedural style, where would that same depositing code live?
options: Inside the balance variable itself
Procedural style cannot change a balance at all
Separate from the balance — the balance sits in a variable, and the code reaches in from outside
In a second copy of the balance
questions.explanation: Procedural keeps them apart: variables hold values, statements do work, nothing owns anything.

questions.question: What is the defining feature of procedural programming?
options: It can only be used for very small programs
Data and instructions are separate things
It does not allow variables
It always runs faster than object-oriented code
questions.explanation: Separation is the feature — and it is exactly what the next two paradigms change.

questions.question: When does each style fit best?
options: Procedural is direct and easy to follow for a small job; object-oriented pays off as a program grows
Object-oriented is always better, so procedural is only taught for history
Procedural is for games, object-oriented is for websites
Whichever one you learned first is the right one to keep using
questions.explanation: Neither wins in the abstract. Bundling starts paying once the program is big enough to be annoying without it.
